A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-FE research. All 17 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and regression experiments, component ablations, feature-transfer experiments, noise tests, and feature-generation case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds baseline comparisons, hyperparameter-optimization experiments, prediction-model evaluations, and efficiency and operator analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes candidate indexing from 0..b to 1..b, corrects the score comparison to use sj, and moves UpdateBuffer outside the best-score condition. These are limited revisions to the specified algorithm; the prose still describes score-filtered storage. The core evolutionary framework and complex-operator prompting already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 newly lists Pima Indian Diabetes among evaluation datasets in Table 5 and adds a diabetes-oriented case study in Section 6.2. The 19 classification benchmarks in v2 Table 2 were already covered by v1 Tables 2 and 7. Regression coverage and Gaussian-noise scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: OCTree moves from cited related work to an evaluated comparator across classification benchmarks. The complex-dataset comparison also gains FeatLLM and AutoFeat entries, with AutoFeat reported as failing or exceeding the time threshold; v1 compared those datasets only against OpenFE, CAAFE, and the base model. Regression comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces 400-trial Optuna tuning comparisons and CatBoost/Logistic Regression configurations. Figure 2 changes from raw accuracy on v1's classification subset to normalized results on v2 Table 2 datasets below 10,000 samples, without specifying the normalization formula. Table 2 also broadens its failure criterion to include execution exceeding 12 hours.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether feature-engineering gains survive hyperparameter tuning, examine runtime versus accuracy and operator frequencies, and add a diabetes case study. Refinement trajectories expand from two datasets in v1 Figure 3 to twelve in v2 Figure 12. The noise study and Heart/Breast-W cases are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five random splits with distinct seeds. No changed run count, significance-testing procedure, or uncertainty-estimation method is documented. Revised standard-deviation values in Tables 4 and 6 are result changes.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial comparator, tuning, prediction-model, efficiency, and operator results. Matched benchmark scores largely remain unchanged, but Table 4 revises GPT-based MLP classification from 0.784 ± 0.175 to 0.791 ± 0.029 while Table 8 remains identical. Aggregate uncertainties and ranks also change. PC1's final trajectory ordering reverses: LLM-FE finishes above its no-refinement variant in v1 Figure 3 but below it in v2 Figure 12.

T1.justification: The bilevel optimization objective, serialization expression, and Boltzmann sampling equations are retained. Removing the standalone empirical-risk expression and clarifying sub-training notation do not change the underlying mathematics. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central claims about evolutionary feature engineering and predictive improvements. The introduction and Table 1 newly foreground complex-feature generation and multi-feature refinement, replacing the earlier emphasis on classification/regression support in the comparison matrix.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning benefits complementary to hyperparameter tuning, Pareto efficiency, and the value of complex aggregation operators, including a qualification that operator selection needs refinement. V1's separate scalability-mechanism discussion is removed. The exclusion of regression baselines is now attributed to unavailable implementations rather than inherently classification-only hypothesis spaces.

D1.justification: V2 documents OCTree's implementation source and adaptations to data loading and model initialization, identifies the added Pima dataset, and specifies Optuna random sampling with 400 trials. Section 3.1 clarifies the internal training/validation partition. Existing prompts, island settings, sampling temperature, and resource limits are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Optuna reference and sharpens its positioning against the already-cited OCTree, describing single-rule refinement versus multiple evolutionary candidates. Complex-feature generation receives greater emphasis using the already-cited work on LLMs favoring simple features. Most related work is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. Targeted edits rename hypothesis generation and memory management, condense related-work and results passages, rewrite Section 6.2, reorganize appendices C/D, and relocate the impact and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column format, merges v1 Tables 2 and 7, redesigns Table 1 and Figure 2, and adds tuning, prediction-model, efficiency, operator, and case-study displays. Earlier graphics are relocated, and the refinement trajectories become a twelve-panel figure.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens useful comparison and diagnostic evidence, but introduces material reporting problems. V1's raw ablation accuracy is replaced by insufficiently defined normalization. V2's PC1 plot contradicts its retained interpretation, and the new HPO table's untuned blood-transfusion values conflict with Table 2. Appendix D.1 also claims only the base model is faster, although Figure 9 shows OCTree faster too. These inconsistencies offset the broader evaluation enough that a reliable net quality direction cannot be established.
